article_title: Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation.
citation: Barrit Sami, Ranuzzi Giovanni, Fetzer Steffen, Al Barajraji Mejdeddine, Hadwe Salim El, Zanello Marc, Ortler Martin, O'Flaherty Julieta, Massager Nicolas, Madsen Joseph R., Dibué Maxine, Carron Romain. (2025). Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation. Acta Neurochirurgica. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00701-025-06610-8
title: VNS masterclass MCQ assessment: 14 items with 67 binary propositions scored from -1 to +1 per question
description: The assessment instrument was an MCQ in which "The MCQ consisted of 14 items (Supplemental Material 3) containing 67 assertive propositions", each requiring a binary true/false judgment. Scoring assigned or deducted a fraction of 1/n per proposition, with total scores ranging from -1 (all incorrect) to +1 (all correct) per question, so a score of zero represented performance equivalent to random chance. It was designed by three neurosurgeons and one technical expert to test practical clinical knowledge for safe and effective VNS implementation.
requirements: Questions must test practical clinical knowledge required for safe and effective VNS implementation rather than theoretical or research-oriented concepts, as the faculty designed them
constraints: The authors state that MCQs do not fully capture the complexity of real-world clinical settings
target_learners: board-certified neurosurgeons already performing VNS procedures
target_learning_goals: VNS clinical management, surgical anatomy, procedural steps, and technical aspects
examples: All 36 course attendees completed the assessment after a 2-day masterclass including theoretical instruction, practical workshops, and surgical cadaver-based training
